frequency_question: What proportion of major bilateral trade negotiations between advanced economic blocs and large emerging markets reach a signed agreement within a comparable multi-year window once momentum is established?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral trade agreement negotiations between the European Union or United States and major G20 emerging economies (India, Brazil, ASEAN, Indonesia, etc.) lasting more than 5 years. Excludes minor updates or mini-deals.
window: A 1.5-year observation period corresponding to the timeframe remaining until the deadline.

cases.name: EU-Mercosur (negotiated heavily, stalled/not signed in window)
US-Kenya Strategic Trade and Investment Partnership
EU-India (First round of modern talks resumed, ongoing)

coverage_note: 6 named representative major trade negotiation cycles; believed roughly 10 comparable modern complex negotiations globally.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller bilateral investment treaties (BITs) which have higher completion rates due to lower complexity.
skeleton: 6 major bilateral negotiation instances tracked over historical comparable periods
multiplier: 3 hits out of 6 comparable deep negotiation terminal phases
validity_reason: Trade negotiation dynamics and geopolitical push for diversification remain structurally consistent through the end of the decade.
